To be an automatic firearm, whether that be semi or fully automatic, the weapon must harness some of the energy from the powder charge to cycle the weapon. There's a variety of ways to do that (e.g. recoil, blowback, piston, direct impingement), but the end result is all the same: the bolt is unlocked, the spent round is extracted and ejected, the hammer/striker is recocked, the new round is loaded, and the bolt is relocked.

Revolvers do not utilize the energy of firing a round to cycle the weapon. To fire again, you must manually recock the hammer and rotate the cylinder (a simultaneous operation in all revolvers) to line up the next chamber with the barrel. They are essentially single-shot firearms that get around the slow firing rate by having multiple chambers pre-loaded.
